primary.title: Mysterium Cosmographicum
primary.author: Johannes Kepler
primary.rationale: Kepler's first major astronomical work, outlining his heliocentric model and geometric explanation of planetary orbits. It is a foundational text in the history of astronomy.

primary.title: Astronomia nova
primary.author: Johannes Kepler
primary.rationale: This work presents Kepler's first two laws of planetary motion, derived from his meticulous analysis of Tycho Brahe's data. It is a landmark publication in scientific history.

primary.title: Harmonices Mundi
primary.author: Johannes Kepler
primary.rationale: In this book, Kepler presents his third law of planetary motion and explores the mathematical relationships between celestial bodies, including his famous 'music of the spheres' concept.

secondary.title: Kepler's Witch: An Astronomer's Young Life
secondary.author: Marcus du Sautoy
secondary.rationale: A biographical account focusing on Kepler's early life and the challenges he faced, offering insights into his scientific development and personal circumstances.

secondary.title: The Essential Kepler
secondary.author: Johannes Kepler
secondary.rationale: While this is a collection of Kepler's writings, the scholarly introduction and annotations by the editor, Nick Kollerstrom, provide significant secondary analysis and context for his work.

secondary.title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
secondary.author: Owen Gingerich
secondary.rationale: A foundational article by a leading Kepler scholar, providing a detailed analysis of the development and significance of Kepler's laws.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are likely available in their original Latin or in translation on Internet Archive. Secondary sources are selected for their scholarly merit and recency, with a focus on biographical and analytical works.
